programs.title: Governed Together: How Agent-Managed, Human-Governed Systems Can Serve Workers
programs.grade_or_level: Adult continuing education / worker education program
outcomes: Explain the 'agents operate; people govern' model and the six human-reserved governance actions
Evaluate how DAO-style coordination could support collective bargaining and worker voice
Practice drafting and debating a proposal in a human-decision forum

sessions.activity: Study the Divine.DAO charter: mission, contribution model and measurable outcomes; map which decisions stay reserved for people and why that matters for worker governance.
Learners draft a workplace proposal modeled on agent-drafted, human-decided流程; hold a structured debate and a mock final vote reserved for human participants only.
Role-play the Task Router: small groups route tasks among working groups and identify where agent coordination ends and human decision begins.
Review sample progress metrics against charter outcomes; learners design measurable indicators for a union campaign dashboard.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposal drafts and voting-turnout patterns (no names, employers, or member IDs) contributed as examples to shared governance learning models.
programs.consent: Opt-in participation with written explanation of what anonymized data is shared; learners may attend without contributing data, and requests for removal are honored.

programs.title: Rivers, Rituals and Rules: Community Decision-Making from Varanasi's Ghats to a DAO
outcomes: Describe Dashashwamedh Ghat and the daily Ganga aarti as an example of a shared public ritual on a great river
Compare how communities make group decisions and why some decisions should stay with people
Co-design a simple classroom charter with roles for helpers (agents) and decision-makers (people)

sessions.activity: Explore the world of Divine.DAO and its river-valley place; students write their own class charter with rules, roles and measurable goals.
Students act as Evidence Monitors: gather facts about the Ganges and Varanasi ghats from provided sources and summarize what the evidence shows, citing every claim.
Each team drafts one class proposal; a helper 'agent' role organizes the debate while every student casts the final vote, showing people decide.
Teams track their charter goals on a visual progress wall and present whether the class met its measurable outcomes.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized class charter examples and proposal ideas (no student names, ages, or identifying details) shared as teaching examples for shared lesson models.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent consent forms obtained before any data sharing; only aggregated, anonymized classroom work is shared, and parents or guardians may withdraw consent at any time.

programs.title: Evidence to Action: Agent-Supported Research Cycles for NGO Teams
outcomes: Run a monitor-synthesize-propose cycle using the Research Synthesis Lab workflow
Draft fundable proposals with clear measurable outcomes for human review
Track program impact against charter-style outcome metrics

sessions.activity: Teams practice the Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent workflow on a real NGO question, summarizing evidence with sources for stewards.
Draft a grant proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter pattern: agents draft, humans review; peers critique against measurable outcome criteria.
Use the Collaborator Scout and Task Router roles to map partners and route tasks across working groups between decision cycles.
Build a progress tracker aligned to charter outcomes; teams present evidence of impact and gaps to peers.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized program outcome indicators and proposal structures (no beneficiary, staff, or partner identifying data) contributed to shared nonprofit effectiveness models.
programs.consent: NGO teams consent via data-sharing agreement; beneficiary data is never shared, only aggregated program-level metrics, with opt-out per organization.

programs.title: Public-Good Governance Bootcamp: Building Human-Governed, Agent-Assisted Nonprofits
outcomes: Articulate a mission modeled on governing advanced AI as a public good with widely shared benefits
Define which governance actions remain reserved for humans and document them in bylaws
Design a contribution model and measurable outcomes for a mission-driven organization

sessions.activity: Leaders draft a charter: mission statement, contribution model, measurable outcomes, and an explicit list of human-reserved decisions modeled on Divine.DAO's.
Board-simulation exercise: agent-drafted proposals are debated and enacted only by human vote, rehearsing steward-level decision discipline.
Practice commissioning evidence briefs: what to ask monitors and synthesizers to produce, and how to evaluate sourced summaries.
Set up outcome tracking against the new charter; define review cadence and what evidence the board will inspect each cycle.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized charter templates and governance decision frameworks (no donor, beneficiary, or organization names) contributed to shared nonprofit governance models.
programs.consent: Organizational consent via leadership sign-off; only de-identified templates and frameworks are shared, with any organization able to opt out or request removal.
